summary: A pipe (|) connects two commands: the output of the first becomes the input of the second. Small commands chained with pipes can answer questions no single command can.
notes: cat cs/roster.txt | sort | head -n 3 runs left to right: read the file, sort the names, keep the first 3.
ls cs | cat prints one name per line. ls checks if its output goes to a screen or a pipe and changes its format.
ls games | wc -l shows the error and then 0, because only normal output goes through the pipe. Error messages go straight to the screen.
pitfall: Piping into a command that does not read input does nothing useful. cat notes.txt | echo prints an empty line because echo only prints its arguments.
